newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel court rejects petition to charge Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Israel court rejects petition to charge Netanyahu.

text.p: Israel's High Court on Sunday rejected a petition demanding that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu be indicted for fraud and breach of trust in a government corruption scandal.
Four judges on the five-member panel voted to throw out opposition lawmakers' petition to overrule a decision by state prosecutors not to charge Netanyahu.
"The court does not intervene in decisions of the state attorney unless they are extremely unreasonable," High Court Justice Yitzhak Zamir told the court.

In a minority opinion which could generate further criticism of Netanyahu in the scandal that threatened to bring down his government, one judge wanted to issue an injunction ordering the state attorney to show cause for his decision not to indict the prime minister.

"The minority decision is that the evidence collected in this affair, and the importance of the matter, justify issuing a temporary injunction concerning the decision not to indict the prime minister," said Justice Dalia Dorner.
The court also rejected a petition to indict Justice Minister Tsahi Hanegbi.

Israeli police, after a months-long probe, had recommended both Netanyahu and Hanegbi be charged with fraud and breach of trust in the short-lived appointment of lawyer Roni Bar-On as attorney-general in January.

Israel's Channel One Television had alleged Bar-On's appointment was part of a deal to win a plea bargain for key coalition legislator Aryeh Deri of the religious Shas party in his three-year corruption trial.
But state prosecutors on April 20 said there was sufficient evidence to indict only Deri.
Attorney General Elyakim Rubinstein said the police case against Netanyahu was based on testimony of one witness which he said was insufficient for bringing charges.
Deri has denied all accusations. Bar-On, who quit 12 hours after taking office amid a public outcry that he was unqualified for the job, was cleared by prosecutors.
Israeli opposition legislators swiftly appealed against the prosecutors' decision.

At a hearing last month, the five-judge panel threw out several related petitions including a request to order a state investigation into the allegations and one to make public the 995-page police report on the affair.
Netanyahu apologised for any mistakes in the Bar-On appointment, but accused the media and opposition of trying to use the affair to overthrow the government.
